question: For which song did Tanvi Shah become the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award in 2010?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jai Ho**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tanvi Shah** became the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award in 2010 for her contribution to the song **"Jai Ho."**
 
• The song "Jai Ho" was a part of the soundtrack for the movie **"Slumdog Millionaire"**, directed by Danny Boyle.
 
• The track was composed by **A.R. Rahman**, with lyrics by Gulzar and vocals by Sukhwinder Singh, Tanvi Shah, and Mahalaxmi Iyer.
 
• "Jai Ho" won the **Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media** at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards.
 
• The song also earned the **Academy Award for Best Original Song** in 2009, further cementing its global recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tanvi Shah:**

 
 
• An Indian playback singer known for her work in multiple languages, including Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu.
 
• She is recognized for her versatility and unique vocal texture, contributing to numerous hit songs across industries.
 
 
 
• **Slumdog Millionaire:**
 
 
• A British-Indian drama film directed by Danny Boyle and co-directed in India by Loveleen Tandan.
 
• The movie won eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, and was a critical and commercial success worldwide.
 
 
 
• **A.R. Rahman:**
 
 
• A globally acclaimed Indian composer, singer, and music producer, often referred to as the "Mozart of Madras."
 
• He has won multiple awards, including two Academy Awards, two Grammy Awards, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe.
 
 
 
• **Grammy Awards:**
 
 
• One of the most prestigious music awards globally, presented by the Recording Academy to recognize outstanding achievements in the music industry.
 
• The awards cover various categories, including classical, pop, rock, and visual media soundtracks.
